description: A knight in full mail pushes through the front doors, hand on sword, spurs ringing on stone. The hall goes quiet. They stop in front of you and issue a formal challenge—combat for honor and coin, right here, right now.

choices.option: Accept the duel. (Risk: Worker Health; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success:
[acting_worker] meets every blow clean, steel on steel. The knight pushes hard but can't break through. After the final exchange both step back, breathing heavy, grinning.

The knight pulls off their helm and offers a toast. Honor satisfied, purse earned ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] can't keep up. Every parry lands late, every counter falls short. The knight batters them back until blood shows through torn cloth. You cover the medical costs and the knight's fee while the crowd mutters about your house fielding amateurs ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -10 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Decline, but offer the knight free drinks. (Cost: Money; Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You wave off the duel and offer the knight your best table instead. Their entourage settles in, orders flow, and by closing time the knight is buying rounds for the house. The drinks cost you, but the goodwill is worth it ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

description: Crude flyers plastered across every post in the district—your name mocked in bad verse, your guild drawn as a joke. The rival guild's seal is still wet. Passersby stop to read and glance your way. You need to respond or let this stand.

choices.option: Send a worker to publicly refute the taunts. (Risk: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] plants themselves under the biggest flyer and starts tearing the rival's claims apart, point by point. The crowd gathers, laughs build, and by the end people are cheering your guild's name. The rival's insults backfire completely ({actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] stumbles over their own words and the crowd turns on them fast. The rival guild's people are ready with heckles, and every fumbled line makes it worse. By the time your worker retreats, your guild is the district's punchline ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Ignore the taunts. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You tell your people to ignore it and get back to work. The flyers stay up, unanswered. Some folk start wondering if the rival guild might have a point. Silence has a cost ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A patron is tearing through their pockets, overturning cushions, voice cracking. They lost a family heirloom somewhere on your premises—irreplaceable, generations old. Other guests are watching. How you handle this will be remembered.

choices.option: Assign a worker to search for it. (Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] retraces the patron's steps methodically—checks the benches, the floor, the coat hooks. There it is, wedged under a seat in the back. A scratched silver locket, older than anyone in the room. The patron breaks down in relief and presses a heavy purse into your worker's hands. Word spreads fast ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] checks every corner, every surface—nothing. The heirloom is gone. The patron leaves in silence, and the other guests watch them go. Word gets around that things go missing at your place ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Offer condolences but do nothing. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You offer sympathetic words but don't lift a finger. The patron searches your face for something more, finds nothing, and gathers their things. The other guests notice. A place that won't help when it matters loses trust quietly ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: Someone grabbed a magical herb instead of common seasoning. The main course is glowing, humming with arcane energy, and the dining room is split between fascinated and terrified. Plates are literally pulsing with light. You need to act fast.

choices.option: Market it as a magical delicacy. (Risk: Reputation; Potential: Money)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] strides out of the kitchen with the glowing dish held high and sells it hard—rare magical delicacy, once-in-a-lifetime experience. The patrons buy it completely. Coin pours in, nobles start asking when you'll serve it again, and the waiting list grows before the night is over ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] tries to sell it, but their nerves show. Patrons see danger, not novelty—chairs scrape, people head for the exits. The dining room empties fast, and by morning the district is calling your kitchen cursed ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Apologize and comp everyone's meals. (Cost: Money; Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You pull the glowing plates, apologize to every table, and declare the night's meals free. It stings your purse, but the patrons appreciate the honesty. By closing, most are laughing about it. Your reputation for doing right by the customer holds ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A sharp-eyed stranger is cleaning out your tables on an impossible winning streak. Coins keep flowing their way and the regulars are getting nervous. Could be skill, could be cheating, could be something worse. Either way, the house is bleeding gold.

choices.option: Have a skilled dealer take over. (Risk: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] takes over the table with steady hands and a sharp eye. They read the stranger's patterns, shift the pace, and the streak breaks. The crowd watches the house claw its money back hand by hand. By the final round, the stranger folds and the regulars are cheering ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] can't crack it. Every play feeds the stranger's pile, and the crowd goes quiet as your house gold drains away. The stranger leaves with a fat purse and a grin. You're left counting losses and fielding uncomfortable questions from regulars ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Let the game proceed normally. (Risk: Money)
choices.message: You let the game run its course. The streak cools on its own eventually—it always does. The stranger walks out with a decent profit and a knowing smile. Losses are manageable, and at least nobody can say you interfered ({actual_money}).

description: A well-dressed client arrives after dark, all silk and quiet confidence. They pull you aside and make a specific request—private company for the evening, someone exceptional. The coin they flash is real. The question is whether you can deliver.

choices.option: Assign your best charmer. (Potential: Money)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] reads the client perfectly—right tone, right pace, effortless warmth. The evening goes exactly as it should. A heavy purse changes hands at the end, along with a promise to return. Word of your house's quality reaches the right circles ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] tries, but the chemistry isn't there. The client stays polite, the evening stays flat, and it ends early. A modest fee for the time, but the real money walks out the door ({actual_money}, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Politely decline the request. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You explain that nobody is available tonight. The client nods, but the look says they expected better. They leave without a fuss—and without coming back. Their coin will go to a competitor ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: An unsigned package arrives at dawn—expensive wrapping, no seal, no name. Inside: a valuable gift and a note written in a shaky hand, clearly from someone with deep pockets and deeper feelings. The sender wants to stay anonymous.

choices.option: Have the worker investigate the sender. (Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] works the clues—ribbon quality, parchment type, handwriting style—and traces the gift back to a shy noble too nervous to introduce themselves. Handled with discretion, the noble is grateful and generous. A fat purse arrives the next day with a thank-you note ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] asks too many questions in too many places. The gossip spreads before the answer does. The admirer pulls back completely, and now your establishment has a reputation for not knowing when to leave things alone ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Accept the gift and ignore the note. (Potential: Money)
choices.message: You pocket the gift, let [acting_worker] enjoy it, and leave the mystery alone. The sender stays anonymous and probably appreciates that. Easy money, no drama ({actual_money}, +5 Joy).

description: A wealthy patron claims the best seat in the house and requests a private dance—veils, music, the full show. They have coin to back the ask and high expectations. Deliver, and the payout is serious. Fall short, and they'll talk.

choices.option: Assign a worker to perform. (Potential: Money; Risk: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] owns the floor from the first step. Every movement is deliberate, every veil timed perfectly. The patron sits frozen, barely breathing. When the last veil drops the room erupts—applause, coin on the table, requests for a repeat. Word of the performance spreads fast ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] starts strong but loses the rhythm at the worst moment. The tension breaks, the patron's interest fades, and the room goes flat. They leave politely, but the disappointment is obvious. That kind of review travels ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Refuse the request. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You turn them down flat—your call, your house. The patron doesn't argue, but the displeasure is plain. They leave quietly, coin and all. That money will end up at a competitor's place by the end of the night ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A traveling bard starts playing something slow, raw, and unmistakably sultry. Conversations die. Patrons lean in. The mood in the room shifts hard—drinks are flowing and the atmosphere is charged. You can ride this wave or shut it down.

choices.option: Encourage a worker to join in. (Potential: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] steps up and joins the bard mid-verse. Their voices lock together and the whole room holds its breath. When the last note rings out, the applause is deafening. Drinks flow, tips pile up, and your tavern's name gets attached to a night people won't forget ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] tries to join in and misses the key completely. The mood breaks, patrons cringe, and the bard shoots you a look that could curdle ale. The evening's momentum is gone. People finish their drinks and leave early ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Ask the bard to play something less... stimulating. (Cost: Money; Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You pay the bard to switch to something tamer. The mood cools, conversations resume, and the energy drains out of the room. Purses stay closed for the rest of the night. Safe choice, but it cost you ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

description: Someone at the back table whispers the word 'plague' and the room freezes. A patron claims one of your workers looks pale, shaky, wrong. Within minutes half your customers are eyeing the door. The rumor is almost certainly baseless, but fear doesn't wait for facts.

choices.option: Pay a local healer to publicly examine the worker. (Cost: Money; Risk: Reputation)
choices.message_success: The healer checks [acting_worker] in front of the whole room—pulse, eyes, throat—and announces a clean bill of health. The crowd exhales. A few patrons order another round. Your quick response earns respect across the district ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: The healer clears [acting_worker], but the damage is done. Some patrons nod and stay. Others mutter that healers can be bought and slip out anyway. The rumor fades slowly, but tonight's empty tables tell their own story ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Dismiss the rumor as nonsense. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You wave it off publicly and tell everyone to get back to their drinks. Some do. Others exchange glances and leave early. Several tables stay empty for the rest of the night ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: Your regular supplier shows up with ledgers in hand and a sour expression. They spread parchments across your table, pointing at line items and overdue balances. The numbers are debatable, but the frustration isn't.

choices.option: Have a worker renegotiate terms. (Potential: Money; Risk: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] sits down with the supplier and talks it through—acknowledges the backlog, offers a revised schedule, finds middle ground. Both sides sign off satisfied ({actual_money}).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] pushes too hard and the conversation turns heated. The supplier leaves with their trust shaken. Other merchants hear about it before the day is out ({actual_reputation} reputation).

choices.option: Pay a rush fee. (Cost: Money)
choices.message: You produce the coin and settle the balance on the spot. The supplier's expression softens immediately. Not the cheapest solution, but the partnership holds ({actual_money}).

description: A wooden crate with someone else's name on it sits at your doorstep. The delivery boy is long gone. The rightful owner's address is clearly marked, but the iron bands and wax seals hint at something valuable inside.

choices.option: Return the crate to its rightful owner. (Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You send [acting_worker] to deliver the crate where it belongs. The owner is grateful and vocal about it—your name gets mentioned in the merchant quarter ({actual_reputation} reputation).

choices.option: Check contents before deciding. (Risk: Reputation; Potential: Money)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] inspects the contents carefully without breaking the seals. Useful supplies, exactly what you needed. The crate reaches its owner eventually, but not before you skim a small profit ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] gets caught poking through the crate by a passing merchant who recognizes the owner's seal. Word spreads fast ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

choices.option: Quietly absorb the supplies. (Gain: Money; Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: The crate disappears into your storage. Profit goes up, but certain merchants start giving you sideways looks ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A contact pulls you aside and speaks in low tones. The governor's real protection isn't soldiers or gold—it's a bound djinn, sealed with blood and starlight. Only one thing can break that bond: a Binding Gem of purest crystal, rare and ruinously expensive.

choices.option: Follow the rumor to its source.
choices.message: You commit the details to memory. Somewhere in the city's hidden markets or guild vaults, a Binding Gem can be found. The governor's supernatural protection has a weakness—you just need the right leverage.

description: A hooded contact steps out of the crowd and opens their palm. A crystal pulses with faint inner light—unmistakably a Binding Gem. They won't sell it outright. They want proof you're worth dealing with first.

choices.option: Sway the contact. (Requires Charm)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] talks them around—steady voice, right promises, enough charm to build trust without overdoing it. The Binding Gem changes hands willingly.
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] makes their case, but the contact isn't convinced. The Binding Gem stays in their pocket. You'll need another approach.

choices.option: Prove your mettle. (Requires Combat)
choices.message_success: Steel rings in the alley. [acting_worker] meets the contact's test blow for blow—quick, controlled, decisive. The contact yields with a nod of respect and hands over the Binding Gem.
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] fights well but not well enough. The contact disengages and shakes their head. The Binding Gem stays out of reach for now.

description: An apothecary pulls their cart up to your door, loaded with tonics and remedies at bulk prices. The merchant claims they over-brewed and need to move stock fast—good deal if the quality holds.

choices.option: Buy the batch outright. (Cost: Money)
choices.message: You pay and stock the lot. The tonics are solid—useful for workers and patrons alike ({actual_money}).

choices.option: Negotiate a better rate. (Risk: Reputation; Potential: Money)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] chats up the apothecary, finds common ground, and talks the price down without souring the deal ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] pushes too hard on price. The apothecary's expression sours, and other merchants nearby overhear ({actual_reputation} reputation).

choices.option: Decline politely.
choices.message: You pass on the offer. The apothecary nods and rolls their cart onward. Not every deal needs taking.

description: A city official steps through your door with a ledger and the expression of someone looking for violations. They scan the room, note the entertainment, and ask to see your performance licenses.

choices.option: Have a worker demonstrate decorum and compliance. (Potential: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] walks the official through your operation—clean records, organized setup, professional conduct. The inspector's stern face softens. Your establishment passes with commendation ({actual_reputation} reputation).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] tries their best, but the official isn't impressed. They leave without a citation but without approval either ({actual_reputation} reputation).

choices.option: Pay the routine fee. (Cost: Money)
choices.message: You hand over the documentation and the fee. The official stamps your papers and moves on. Quick and painless ({actual_money}).

description: Last night's storm left a gift: a steady drip running down the back wall. Small now, but water and wood don't mix well over time. You need to decide how seriously to take it before the rot sets in.

choices.option: Repair properly. (Cost: Money; Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You bring in proper craftsmen who replace the damage and reinforce what was weak. It costs real coin, but the building is stronger for it ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

choices.option: Quick patch for now. (Cost: Money; Risk: Reputation)
choices.message: Pitch and rags stop the drip. Cheap and fast, but observant patrons glance at the patch job ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

choices.option: Close a corner of the room. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You rope off the wet section and rearrange seating. It works, but the room feels smaller and regulars ask questions ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A scarred warrior enters and the room goes quiet. They move with the controlled ease of someone who has survived more fights than most people have had meals. Their gaze locks onto one of your workers. 'I seek someone worthy to inherit my art. The blade demands everything—those who endure gain power few can match.'

choices.option: Accept the Blademaster's trial. (Requires Combat 65+)
choices.message_success: Three days without rest. Blade forms until muscles give out, sparring against a master who holds nothing back, meditation that forges focus into steel. When it ends, [acting_worker] moves differently—strikes land with new precision, footwork flows without thought. The Blademaster nods once and disappears. A true Blademaster has been made.
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] steps up, but the Blademaster ends the test after a single exchange. 'Your spirit is strong. Your blade isn't ready. Train harder—we may meet again.' They leave without looking back.

choices.option: Politely decline the offer.
choices.message: You thank the warrior but explain your workers have other duties. 'The blade chooses its own time,' they say, and leave.

description: An elderly figure appears in your establishment without using the door. Glowing runes orbit their robes and wine glasses hum faintly. 'I have traveled far seeking one touched by magic,' the archmage says. 'True potential is rare—rarer still is someone worthy of what I carry. Is there such a soul among you?'

choices.option: Present a magical worker for training. (Requires Clever 65+ and 'Magical' trait)
choices.message_success: The archmage's eyes widen as [acting_worker] approaches. 'Yes—this one burns bright.' What follows is not teaching but awakening—ancient words spoken into the mind, visions of currents beneath reality, doors opening in consciousness. When the archmage departs, magic is no longer something [acting_worker] does. It is something they are. They have become an Arcane Adept.
choices.message_failure: The archmage probes [acting_worker]'s essence carefully, then shakes their head. 'The potential exists, but the foundation is too thin. Master the basics first.' They vanish in a flash of light.

choices.option: Admit you have no one suitable.
choices.message: You tell the archmage no one here has the aptitude. They nod. 'Magic finds its own vessels in time.' They fade from sight.

description: You don't see them arrive. One moment the corner booth is empty; the next, a hooded figure sits there. Their face stays hidden despite bright lamps. 'The Shadow Guild has been watching,' they say. 'We need new blood—someone quick and sharp who understands darkness is a tool, not a threat.'

choices.option: Recommend an agile worker for initiation. (Requires Agility 65+)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] approaches without hesitation, and something passes between them—recognition. The figure produces a black silk blindfold. 'The training begins now.' [acting_worker] puts it on and melts into the shadows. Days later, they return changed—movements fluid, presence harder to notice. They have become a Shadowdancer.
choices.message_failure: The figure watches [acting_worker] approach, then shakes their head. 'Eager, but not ready.' They press a black coin into [acting_worker]'s hand. 'Train. When you're ready, you'll know how to find us.' Then they're gone.

choices.option: Refuse to deal with the Shadow Guild.
choices.message: You decline firmly. The figure tilts their head. 'Caution has its merits. The shadows will remember your choice.' When you blink, they're gone.

description: Golden light fills the doorway before the visitor steps inside. Patrons straighten as a figure in white robes enters—where they walk, aches ease and moods lift. 'I am guided by divine providence,' the high priest says. 'One among you carries a pure heart worthy of celestial blessing.'

choices.option: Present a worthy worker for blessing. (Requires Charm 65+)
choices.message_success: The high priest's eyes light up as [acting_worker] approaches. 'Yes—this is the one.' Hands on [acting_worker]'s head, chanting in a language older than kingdoms. Golden light suffuses their form. When the ritual ends, [acting_worker] radiates warmth that draws people close, and minor wounds heal faster in their presence. They have become Divine Touched.
choices.message_failure: The high priest studies [acting_worker] carefully, then sighs. 'The heart is good, but there's too much conflict within for the blessing to take root. Find peace first.' They depart with a gentle benediction.

choices.option: Thank them but decline.
choices.message: You say your workers are content as they are. The high priest smiles. 'The divine gift is not diminished by hesitation.' They bless the room and depart.

description: The door opens and the smell of pine fills the room. A lean figure enters—leather and fur, hawk-sharp eyes that catalog every exit in a single sweep. An ancient bow across their back. 'I seek a student. Someone who can read the wind, track prey across stone, and strike true when it matters.'

choices.option: Offer a capable worker for training. (Requires Agility 65+)
choices.message_success: The ranger master studies [acting_worker] with predator intensity, then nods. 'Come. We begin now.' Weeks of grueling wilderness training follow—tracking across impossible terrain, surviving off the land, moving without trace. When [acting_worker] returns, their eyes catch what others miss, their feet find paths where none exist. They have become a true Pathfinder.
choices.message_failure: The ranger master watches [acting_worker] attempt basic tracking, then frowns. 'Your spirit is willing, but your body hasn't learned to listen to the wild.' They hand over a carved wolf-head token. 'Train until you can cross a forest without disturbing a leaf. Then find me.'

choices.option: Explain you have no suitable candidates.
choices.message: You tell the ranger none of your workers fit. They nod. 'The wild calls to few. Perhaps our paths cross again.' They leave as silently as they arrived.

description: An old figure shuffles in on a gnarled walking stick—easy to dismiss as just another tired traveler. Then the regulars go quiet. This is Old Morrow, the legendary barkeep who once served drinks at the capital’s finest houses, said to read people well enough to prevent wars. They settle onto a stool and rasp: ‘I’d share what I know with someone who truly sees people. Is there such a soul here?’

choices.option: Present a promising worker to Old Morrow. (Requires Service 65+)
choices.message_success: Old Morrow’s eyes sharpen as [acting_worker] approaches. ‘You have it. The gift of seeing.’ Long nights of quiet conversation follow—not how to pour drinks, but how to read the tension in a patron’s shoulders, the meaning behind their order, the story in the calluses on their hands. When Morrow vanishes one morning without farewell, [acting_worker] discovers they possess Barkeep’s Wisdom. They see people in ways they never imagined.
choices.message_failure: Old Morrow studies [acting_worker], then shakes their head. ‘The seed is there, but it hasn’t sprouted. You watch people, but you don’t see them—not yet.’ They press a worn copper coin into [acting_worker]’s palm. ‘Hold this when you meet someone new. Ask yourself what they’re really saying. Come back when you know.’

choices.option: Thank them but explain you cannot spare anyone.
choices.message: You respectfully decline, citing the demands of running your place. Old Morrow chuckles. ‘Running a tavern well is its own wisdom.’ They finish a drink you never poured and shuffle out into the night.

description: The door slams open and the figure standing there needs no introduction—their face is on tavern signs and storybooks across the realm. A hero of the Shadow Wars, still wearing the battered armor that once held the front line. They survey the room and break into a grin. ‘Finally, a proper drinking house. But I’m not just here for ale—I’m looking for someone with the spark. Someone who could become what I once was.’

choices.option: Introduce your most battle-ready worker. (Requires Combat 65+)
choices.message_success: The hero’s eyes sharpen as [acting_worker] steps forward—weight balanced, gaze steady, hands loose. ‘There it is. Steel under the skin.’ Training follows: stance and spacing, timing a blow, and—rarer still—how to hold a shaken line with nothing but voice and example. When the hero departs after many drinks and stories, [acting_worker] stands differently. They have become a People’s Champion—someone others instinctively trust to stand between them and harm.
choices.message_failure: The hero asks [acting_worker] to mirror a simple guard stance and exhales through their teeth. ‘Brave heart. Slow hands.’ They clap [acting_worker] on the shoulder hard enough to stagger them. ‘Come back when your reflexes match your nerve—people don’t follow hesitation into the dark.’

choices.option: Simply offer them drinks and conversation.
choices.message: You serve the hero as a guest rather than disturb your staff. They tell stories until dawn, leave an enormous tip, and promise to return. ‘A good establishment, this. Run by someone who knows their priorities.’ Sometimes that’s worth more than training.

description: A haunting melody fills the room before its source appears—an unassuming figure with a lute older than most kingdoms. This is the Wandering Muse, whose songs have toppled tyrants and, some say, moved the gods to tears. They settle in a corner and play softly. ‘I’ve sung in a thousand taverns. But I grow old, and my stories need new voices. Is there one here who understands the best tales are lived, not told?’

choices.option: Recommend your most eloquent worker. (Requires Charm 65+)
choices.message_success: The Muse’s music shifts to warm approval as [acting_worker] approaches. ‘You understand already.’ The training is unlike anything else—not technique, but truth. How to find the tale in any moment, how to weave words that touch hearts directly, how to make listeners forget they’re listening. When the Muse moves on, [acting_worker] discovers they have become a Tale Weaver. Their words now carry power beyond mere entertainment.
choices.message_failure: The Muse plays a melancholic note and studies [acting_worker]. ‘You have words, but not yet the wisdom to wield them. You tell stories at people, not for them.’ A final lingering chord. ‘Listen more. Speak less. When you can hear the story someone needs before they know it themselves, find me.’

choices.option: Ask them to simply perform for your patrons.
choices.message: You request only a performance. The Muse obliges with a concert your patrons will talk about for years. ‘Art freely given is never wasted,’ they say before departing. Your reputation climbs, and somehow everyone who attended seems a little wiser.

description: A carriage bearing the royal crest stops outside. From it emerges Master Ambrose Laurent, former head chef of the royal kitchens, whose dishes were served at the coronation of three monarchs. He surveys your restaurant with a critical eye. ‘I have eaten at every notable establishment in the realm and found them adequate.’ His gaze softens. ‘But I sense potential here. Raw talent that could be refined. Is there someone in your kitchen with true fire?’

choices.option: Present your most dedicated kitchen worker. (Requires Service 65+)
choices.message_success: Master Laurent watches [acting_worker] prepare a simple dish with focus, then nods—almost imperceptibly. ‘You. Come.’ Months of brutal training follow: coaxing impossible flavors from humble ingredients, presenting dishes as art, understanding that cooking touches the soul. When Laurent finally pronounces them ‘acceptable’—unprecedented praise—[acting_worker] has become a Master Chef. Their dishes now evoke memories, heal heartaches, and create moments of pure transcendence.
choices.message_failure: Master Laurent tastes [acting_worker]’s preparation and sets down the fork precisely. ‘Competent. But competence is the enemy of greatness.’ He produces a jar of rare saffron. ‘When you can tell me—without tasting—what memory this spice will evoke in the person who eats it, you’ll be ready.’ He leaves without another word.

choices.option: Simply prepare your finest meal for them.
choices.message: You focus on serving Master Laurent as a guest. He dines in contemplative silence and offers a single nod at the end. ‘You understand hospitality. That is rarer than you think.’ He leaves an enormous tip and a notebook of solid recipes. Sometimes being taken seriously is the greatest compliment.

description: An elegant figure enters with the bearing of royalty, though she wears the simple uniform of service. This is Countess Vermillion Ashford, who renounced her title to pursue wine. Her palate is legendary—she once identified not just a wine’s vineyard and vintage but the mood of the vintner who made it. ‘I travel seeking those with the gift of taste,’ she says, sniffing the air. ‘True taste is not learned but awakened.’

choices.option: Bring forward a worker with refined sensibilities. (Requires Clever 65+)
choices.message_success: The Countess puts [acting_worker] through a series of increasingly complex tastings. Their eyes widen with each revelation as dormant abilities awaken. ‘Yes. You have it—the Perfect Palate.’ Intensive training follows: how flavors interact, how presentation shapes perception, how to pair experiences as much as ingredients. When the Countess departs, pressing a rare vintage into [acting_worker]’s hands, they possess an almost supernatural sensitivity. Every meal becomes a journey.
choices.message_failure: The Countess watches [acting_worker]’s attempts at wine identification with gentle patience. ‘Your mind is willing, but your palate still speaks in simple words. It must learn poetry.’ She leaves a small bottle of herb-infused water. ‘Drink this each morning for a month. It will clarify things.’

choices.option: Offer her your finest wines and request recommendations.
choices.message: You treat the Countess as a guest and consultant. She samples your offerings with pleasure, provides detailed notes on each, and suggests pairings that transform your menu. She leaves a list of suppliers that will significantly improve your stock—knowledge worth its weight in gold.

description: The restaurant falls silent as Sebastian Crane enters—former head butler of the Imperial Household. His posture alone defines the concept of uprightness. He moves through your space with an eye that misses nothing: a water spot on a glass, a setting one degree off-true, a server’s tie slightly askew. ‘I have trained servants who now serve kings,’ he says. ‘I seek raw talent—someone who can learn to anticipate, to become invisible yet indispensable.’

choices.option: Recommend your most attentive server. (Requires Service 65+)
choices.message_success: Crane observes [acting_worker] through several service cycles, expression blank. Then, almost imperceptibly, he nods. ‘You may have potential.’ Rigorous training follows—reading body language, anticipating needs before they’re expressed, moving through spaces without disturbing the air. When Crane finally pronounces them ‘adequate’—his highest praise—[acting_worker] has become a Graceful Server. Their service now feels like magic: needs met before they’re known, comfort provided before it’s sought.
choices.message_failure: Crane watches [acting_worker]’s service with analytical precision. ‘Your technical skills are acceptable. Your presence is not.’ He produces a small bell. ‘Ring this and approach me. I should not hear you coming nor see you until you wish to be seen. Practice until you can surprise me.’ He departs without a sound.

choices.option: Request only his feedback on your service standards.
choices.message: You ask for professional consultation. Crane spends an evening observing and then delivers devastatingly accurate feedback on every aspect of your service. His suggestions, once implemented, dramatically improve customer satisfaction. ‘A good establishment knows when to seek expertise,’ he says before departing.

description: The whole casino holds its breath as a figure enters wearing a smile that has won and lost fortunes. This is ‘Lucky’ Mathias Cross, the gambler who once won a duchy in a single hand—then gave it back because ‘owning things is boring.’ His presence causes other gamblers to flee or crowd close. He settles at a table. ‘Fortune is not random. It’s a conversation. I can teach someone to speak its language.’

choices.option: Introduce a perceptive worker to Lucky. (Requires Clever 65+)
choices.message_success: ‘Lucky’ Mathias studies [acting_worker] across a series of hands, missing nothing. Then he laughs—genuine delight. ‘You see it, don’t you? The patterns in the chaos.’ Lessons follow in perception: reading shifts in probability, sensing when luck is about to turn, knowing when to push and when to fold. When Mathias moves on, [acting_worker] has become Fortune’s Favorite—possessing an uncanny sense for timing and probability in all aspects of life.
choices.message_failure: Mathias studies [acting_worker]’s play and shakes his head. ‘You think too much. Fortune speaks in whispers, not logic.’ He flips a coin—it lands on its edge. ‘When you understand why this coin chose neither side, you’ll be ready.’ He vanishes into the crowd.

choices.option: Challenge him to a friendly game yourself.
choices.message: You play against the legend yourself. You lose, of course, but Mathias plays to teach rather than humiliate. ‘You play to win. Try playing to understand.’ He leaves insights about your regular gamblers that prove extremely profitable in the weeks ahead.

description: A hush falls over the card tables as an elderly figure sits down, hands moving with impossible fluidity. This is the Phantom Dealer—identity unknown, reputation immense. They’ve dealt in every major casino in the realm. Cards blur between their fingers. ‘Sixty years of shuffling,’ they say without looking up. ‘Before I retire, I’d pass on what I know. Not to cheat—to master. Anyone here with hands that could learn to sing?’

choices.option: Present a worker with nimble fingers. (Requires Agility 65+)
choices.message_success: The Phantom examines [acting_worker]’s hands with a surgeon’s intensity, then nods. ‘Good bones.’ Months of grueling practice follow—shuffles and cuts repeated thousands of times until they become instinct, card manipulation so precise it borders on art. [acting_worker] learns to feel the cards, know their positions without looking. When the Phantom departs with a final perfect cascade, [acting_worker] has become a Card Shark. Their hands are instruments of impossible precision.
choices.message_failure: The Phantom watches [acting_worker] attempt a basic shuffle and sighs. ‘Your hands want to rush. Cards demand patience.’ They produce the ace of spades. ‘Flip this between your fingers until you can do it without thinking, without looking, without disturbing your breathing. Then find me.’

choices.option: Ask them to demonstrate their skills for entertainment.
choices.message: You request only a performance. The Phantom obliges with a display that draws gasps from even the most jaded gamblers—cards appearing, disappearing, predicting thoughts. The show draws new customers for weeks. ‘Entertainment is its own reward,’ the Phantom says, ‘especially when it pays well.’

description: A figure enters wearing wealth so casually it might be common clothes—but you recognize the cut, the watch worth more than your building. This is Victoria Sterling, the Casino Queen, who built a gambling empire through sheer will and an uncanny eye for valuable patrons. She surveys your operation with calculating eyes. ‘Not all gold glitters equally,’ she says. ‘Some patrons are worth cultivating. I can teach someone to see what I see—if they have the charm to learn.’

choices.option: Introduce your most charismatic worker. (Requires Charm 65+)
choices.message_success: Victoria studies [acting_worker] interacting with patrons, then unexpectedly smiles. ‘You have it. The gift of making people feel special.’ An education in high-stakes hospitality follows—reading wealth through subtle signs, understanding what keeps high rollers returning, making every patron feel like the most important person in the room. When Sterling departs, [acting_worker] has developed the High Roller’s Eye—instinctively identifying valuable patrons and knowing exactly how to earn their loyalty.
choices.message_failure: Victoria observes [acting_worker]’s customer interactions with precision. ‘You’re charming to everyone equally. That’s inefficient.’ She produces a small notebook. ‘Watch the next hundred patrons. Note who spends freely, who hoards, who seeks attention, who seeks escape. Then you’ll begin to understand.’

choices.option: Simply seek her business advice.
choices.message: You ask for consultation rather than training. Victoria spends several hours analyzing your operation and provides pointed recommendations for patron retention and high-value identification. Her advice significantly increases your profits. ‘A wise proprietor invests in wisdom,’ she says before departing.

description: She arrives without fanfare, yet every eye turns. No obvious reason for the magnetism—her dress is elegant but not ostentatious. Yet something about her presence commands the room. This is Madame Celestine, the legendary courtesan whose clients have included emperors and archdukes. ‘I did not build my reputation on beauty alone,’ she says. ‘I built it on understanding. On anticipation.’ Her gaze sweeps your workers. ‘Is there one here who can truly understand another person?’

choices.option: Present your most promising worker. (Requires Sex 65+)
choices.message_success: Celestine observes [acting_worker] with clients over several evenings, then nods. ‘You have the foundation. Now we build the palace.’ An education follows in true companionship—reading desires clients don’t know they have, mastering conversation as foreplay, understanding that seduction happens in the mind first. When Celestine departs, [acting_worker] has achieved Courtesan’s Grace—moving through intimacy with an elegance that transforms physical pleasure into something transcendent.
choices.message_failure: Celestine studies [acting_worker]’s interactions and sighs softly. ‘You see the body but not the soul within it. True intimacy requires seeing both.’ She produces a vial of perfume. ‘Wear this when you work. Let it remind you that every client carries secret gardens. Learn to find the gates.’

choices.option: Simply ask for advice on improving your establishment.
choices.message: You request consultation, and Celestine obliges with insights that transform how you view your business—ambiance, anticipation, the thousand small details separating adequate from extraordinary. Her suggestions dramatically elevate quality. ‘Excellence is in the details,’ she says. ‘And you now know where to look.’

description: Simple robes mark the visitor as a temple initiate, yet their presence fills the room with tangible warmth. A practitioner of the Sacred Touch—an ancient tradition treating physical pleasure as prayer. Their order is nearly extinct. ‘In the old days, we taught that the body is a temple and pleasure the offering. This knowledge must not be lost.’ Their eyes scan your workers. ‘Is there one here ready to learn that touch can be sacred?’

choices.option: Offer your most spiritually inclined worker. (Requires Hand 65+)
choices.message_success: The practitioner places their hands over [acting_worker]’s and closes their eyes. Something passes between them—warmth, recognition. ‘Yes. You can feel it.’ Training follows in sensing energy flow through the body, pressure points that unlock deeper pleasure, techniques refined over millennia. When the practitioner departs to their hidden temple, [acting_worker] has received the Sacred Touch. Their hands carry ancient knowledge, and their ministrations transcend mere physical sensation.
choices.message_failure: The practitioner examines [acting_worker]’s hands, then their eyes. ‘Your body knows the movements, but your spirit is not yet aligned.’ They press a smooth stone into [acting_worker]’s palm. ‘Meditate with this each night. When you can feel its warmth without your hands, you will be ready.’

choices.option: Request they simply bless your establishment.
choices.message: You ask only for a blessing. The practitioner performs a quiet ritual that makes the air warmer and more welcoming. Patrons report feeling inexplicably comforted within your walls. ‘Sacred space creates sacred experiences,’ they say before departing. Business improves noticeably.

description: They appear between one moment and the next—a figure whose presence makes hearts beat faster. This is the Desire Whisperer, a legendary companion who draws out desires clients don’t know they possess. ‘True intimacy is not about the body,’ they say. ‘It is about the words before, the anticipation, the trust that transforms strangers into more.’ Their smile seems meant for everyone at once. ‘Can someone here learn to speak the language of desire?’

choices.option: Present your worker best suited to intimate persuasion. (Requires Oral 65+)
choices.message_success: The Whisperer converses with [acting_worker] for hours—intimate conversations that reveal nothing yet communicate everything. Then they nod. ‘You understand that the most powerful intimacy happens in words.’ Training follows in the art of intimate conversation: questions that unlock hidden desires, the dance of revelation and mystery, anticipation as power. When the Whisperer departs, [acting_worker] has become a fellow Desire Whisperer—able to draw out and fulfill desires clients didn’t know they had.
choices.message_failure: The Whisperer listens to [acting_worker] and smiles gently. ‘You talk to fill silence. You must learn to talk to create hunger.’ They lean close and whisper something that makes [acting_worker] shiver. ‘Remember this feeling. When you can create it with words alone, find me.’

choices.option: Simply enjoy their company as a patron.
choices.message: You engage the Whisperer as a patron. Through conversation alone, they help you understand things about yourself and your business you never consciously recognized. You part feeling more complete, with insights that improve both management and your personal life. ‘Understanding ourselves is the first step to understanding others.’

description: Masked figures shoulder through the side door—too many, too fast, too organized to be drunks. One jams a cudgel under the cashier’s chin while another sweeps chips into a sack. Patrons freeze mid-bet. The leader finds you behind the rail. ‘No guards tonight. That makes this easy. Pay up, or someone learns what happens when a casino forgets steel.’

choices.option: Pay them off before panic spreads. (Loss: Money)
choices.message: You keep your voice level and slide a heavy purse across—enough to sate greed without inviting a return visit. The leader weighs it, signals the others, and they melt back into the street. Tables reopen, but the whispers linger: your casino looked vulnerable tonight ({actual_money}).

choices.option: Send a worker to stand up to them. (Risk: Health; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] steps into the aisle with nothing but nerve—topples a table into the lead robber, scatters the rest before they regroup. A brief, ugly scramble ends with the bandits fleeing into the alley, leaving sacks behind. You still lose some takings to chaos and spooked patrons, but far less than surrender—and word spreads that your house is not undefended ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] throws the first punch and takes the second twice as hard—a weighted club catches them across the ribs. The robbers grab what they can and run laughing. Medics, apologies, and shaken high-rollers cost you dearly. [acting_worker] leaves leaning on someone’s shoulder, pale and bleeding ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -18 Health).

description: A traveling pit fighter kicks open your door, scarred knuckles wrapped in leather, and bellows a challenge to the room. They want a public bout against your best—winner takes a purse collected from the crowd. Patrons are already placing bets.

choices.option: Send a worker to fight. (Risk: Health; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] steps into the ring and reads the pit fighter's rhythm within the first exchange. A feint, a counter, and the visitor hits the floor hard. The crowd roars. Bets pay out in your favor and the pit fighter buys drinks, laughing about the loss ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] takes a heavy hit in the second exchange and doesn't recover. The pit fighter finishes the bout quickly and collects the purse while your worker limps to the back room. The crowd enjoyed the show, but your reputation takes the hit ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -10 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Decline the challenge and offer hospitality instead. (Cost: Money; Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You wave off the fight and invite the pit fighter to drink on the house. They grumble but settle in, and their stories draw a crowd. The evening costs you ale, but the atmosphere stays lively and no one gets hurt ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

description: Three armed thugs block your entrance at dusk, blades visible under their cloaks. Their leader demands a weekly protection fee or promises broken furniture and scared customers. Patrons inside are watching through the windows.

choices.option: Send a worker to confront them. (Risk: Health; Potential: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] walks out alone and doesn't flinch. The first thug swings; [acting_worker] puts them on the ground before the other two can react. The leader backs off, hands raised. Word spreads through the district that your place doesn't bend ({actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] steps out swinging but the thugs fight dirty. A knife slash across the arm ends it fast. You pay their fee this time and patch up your worker while the neighborhood watches ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -10 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Pay them off quietly. (Cost: Money)
choices.message: You hand over the coin without a scene. The thugs pocket it and leave. No blood, no drama, but the taste is bitter. You hope they don't come back, but you know they will ({actual_money}).

choices.option: Threaten to call the city guard. (Risk: Reputation)
choices.message: You mention the guard and the thugs laugh, but they leave. Patrons mutter about how you handled it—some think you looked weak, others think you were smart. The thugs will remember you called their bluff ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A city guard captain enters with two officers and announces an open recruitment trial. Any establishment that fields a strong candidate earns the guard's favor. The captain scans your workers with a practiced eye.

choices.option: Enter a worker in the trial. (Risk: Health; Potential: Reputation, Money)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] steps onto the training ground and matches the guard's drills blow for blow. The captain nods approval at every test—shield work, footwork, endurance. Your worker doesn't join up, but the captain leaves a commendation and a bounty fee for producing quality fighters ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] gets through the first round but falters on the sparring test. The guard officer lands three clean hits and the captain shakes his head. Your establishment's name goes on the wrong list ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Decline and offer the guards refreshments. (Cost: Money; Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You pass on the trial but offer the guards a meal on the house. They accept and spend the afternoon talking well of your place. Not the glory route, but the guard remembers who treats them right ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A worker finds a bundle of trade documents stuffed behind a loose wall panel. The seals look official but the ink is wrong. Someone has been forging paperwork that could implicate your establishment in smuggling if the authorities find them first.

choices.option: Have a worker analyze the documents and trace the forger. (Risk: Reputation; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] studies the forgeries carefully—ink composition, handwriting pressure, seal inconsistencies. They trace it back to a rival's scribe and present the evidence to the merchant guild. The rival pays a steep fine, part of which comes to you as the wronged party ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] digs into the documents but draws the wrong conclusions. The investigation circles back to your place, and a city inspector spends the afternoon asking uncomfortable questions. You clear your name eventually, but not before the damage is done ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Burn the documents and forget about it. (Risk: Reputation)
choices.message: You toss the papers into the fireplace and watch them curl to ash. Problem gone—for now. But whoever planted them might try again, and next time you might not find them first ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A wealthy merchant slaps a heavy coin purse on the counter and grins. They propose a wager: solve their riddle and the purse is yours. Fail, and you owe them a week of free service. The riddle has stumped scholars across three kingdoms.

choices.option: Put a worker forward to solve the riddle. (Risk: Money; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] listens to the riddle twice, stares at the ceiling for a long moment, and delivers the answer with a quiet smile. The merchant's jaw drops. The purse slides across the counter and the crowd breaks into applause. Your place is now known as a house of sharp minds ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] puzzles over the riddle, offers two guesses, and gets both wrong. The merchant collects their winnings with a smirk. Free service for a week means lost revenue, and the regulars won't let your worker forget it ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Decline the wager politely. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You wave off the bet with a smile. The merchant shrugs, pockets the purse, and takes their custom elsewhere. Some patrons look disappointed—they wanted a show ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: The governor's auditor arrives unannounced with a stack of ledgers and a stone-cold expression. They have found discrepancies in your tax filings—numbers that don't add up. You have one chance to explain before the fines start.

choices.option: Have a worker walk the auditor through the books. (Risk: Money; Potential: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] sits down with the auditor and goes line by line. They find the clerical error, show the corrected figures, and present receipts for every transaction in question. The auditor stamps your ledger clean and notes your cooperation. Word reaches the governor's office that your books are solid ({actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] tries to explain the numbers but gets tangled in their own records. The auditor finds two more discrepancies and slaps a fine on the table. Your establishment's name goes on the watch list ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Pay the fine without argument. (Cost: Money)
choices.message: You hand over the fine without making a scene. The auditor pockets the payment and checks your name off the list. Expensive, but at least the matter is closed and you stay off the governor's bad side ({actual_money}).

description: A hooded figure snatches a patron's coin purse and bolts for the back door. The patron screams. The thief is already vaulting over the fence and heading for the rooftops. You have seconds to act before they disappear into the city.

choices.option: Send a worker to chase the thief. (Risk: Health; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] is out the door before anyone else moves. They clear the fence, hit the rooftop tiles at a sprint, and corner the thief three buildings away. The purse comes back, the patron is overjoyed, and the whole district hears about it by morning ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] gives chase but loses footing on the wet tiles. They slide off a low roof and land hard in the alley below. The thief escapes, the patron demands compensation, and your worker needs a healer ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -10 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Compensate the patron from your own pocket. (Cost: Money; Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You let the thief go and cover the patron's loss yourself. They appreciate the gesture, and other patrons notice you take care of your own. The thief gets away, but your reputation holds ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation).

description: An acrobat troupe sets up outside your building, drawing a crowd with flips and catches. Their leader approaches with a proposition: let one of your workers join the finale act tonight, and you keep all the tips collected from the audience.

choices.option: Let a worker join the act. (Risk: Health; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] takes to the routine like they were born in the air. The crowd gasps at every catch and cheers at the landing. Tips rain into the collection hat, and the troupe leader wants to book your place for a return show ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] manages the first few moves but mistimes a catch and tumbles off the platform. The crowd winces. The troupe covers smoothly but the damage is done—your place gets remembered for the fall, not the show ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Decline but let the troupe perform outside. (Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You pass on joining but let the acrobats use your frontage. The crowd drifts inside for drinks after the show. Easy foot traffic without any risk ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A construction scaffold across the street groans and starts to buckle. Timber and tools slide toward a crowd of shoppers below. Someone screams. A fast worker could reach the supports in time or pull people clear before it all comes down.

choices.option: Send a worker to help. (Risk: Health; Potential: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] sprints across the street and shoves three people clear just as the scaffold collapses behind them. Timber crashes where the crowd stood seconds ago. The district watches your worker dust themselves off, unhurt. By evening, your establishment is the talk of the neighborhood ({actual_reputation} reputation, +10 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] rushes in but catches a falling beam across the shoulder. They manage to pull one person clear before going down. The crowd helps, but your worker needs rest and healing. Good intentions, rough outcome ({actual_reputation} reputation, -10 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Call for the city watch instead. (Gain: Reputation)
choices.message: You shout a warning and send someone running for the watch. The crowd scatters in time and no one is seriously hurt. Not as heroic, but no one from your place gets injured either ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A cloaked stranger slides into a booth and spreads a weathered parchment across the table. They claim it leads to a buried cache outside the city walls. The map could be genuine or an elaborate scam. Either way, they want coin for it.

choices.option: Have a worker verify the map's authenticity. (Risk: Money; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] examines the ink, the parchment age, and the landmarks drawn on it. Everything checks out—this is real. You buy the map at a fair price and send a team to the cache. They return with a chest of old coins and a few rare trinkets ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] studies the map and declares it genuine. You buy it. The cache site turns out to be an empty hole someone dug last week. The stranger is long gone with your coin, and your worker's judgment is questioned ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Intimidate the stranger into revealing the truth. (Risk: Reputation; Potential: Money)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] looms over the booth and asks pointed questions with a hand resting on a blade. The stranger cracks fast—the map is real, but they stole it. They hand it over free of charge and bolt. The cache pays off handsomely ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] tries to pressure the stranger, but they call the bluff and make a scene. Other patrons look uncomfortable, and the stranger storms out loudly accusing your place of thuggery. The map was probably fake anyway ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Ignore the stranger entirely. (No effect)
choices.message: You tell the stranger you're not interested in treasure maps. They fold the parchment, shrug, and leave. Maybe it was real, maybe not. Either way, your coin stays in your pocket.

description: A roar shakes the windows. Outside, a scaled beast the size of a cart thrashes free from its cage as a traveling menagerie handler scrambles to contain it. Passersby scatter. The beast is heading toward your building, and the handler is screaming for help.

choices.option: Send a worker to subdue the beast by force. (Risk: Health; Potential: Money, Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] grabs a heavy plank and meets the beast head-on. A solid strike to the snout stuns it long enough for the handler to throw a chain around its neck. The crowd cheers, the handler pays a generous reward, and your place is the hero of the district ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] swings but the beast is faster. A claw rakes across their arm and the beast charges past into a market stall. The handler catches it eventually, but your worker needs stitching and the stall owner blames you ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, -10 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Send a worker to corral the beast back toward its cage. (Risk: Health; Potential: Reputation)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] circles wide, claps loud, and drives the beast back step by step. Quick feet keep them just out of reach while guiding the animal into a dead-end alley where the handler slams the cage shut. No blood, no damage, and the handler is deeply grateful ({actual_money}, {actual_reputation} reputation, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] tries to herd the beast but it turns sharply and clips them with its tail. They go sprawling into a stack of crates. The handler eventually corrals the beast alone, but your worker limps back bruised and embarrassed ({actual_reputation} reputation, -5 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Bar the doors and wait it out. (Loss: Reputation)
choices.message: You lock up and let someone else deal with it. The beast is caught eventually, but people saw you bolt your doors while others helped. Not a great look for the neighborhood ({actual_reputation} reputation).

description: A runner slips you a note with an address and a time. An underground fight ring is running tonight, and they want fresh blood. The purse is fat, the rules are thin, and nobody asks questions about where the fighters come from.

choices.option: Enter a worker in the ring. (Risk: Health; Potential: Money)
choices.message_success: [acting_worker] walks into the pit and the crowd goes quiet. Three rounds later, their opponent is on the floor and the bookmaker is counting out your winnings. Your worker walks out with bruises and a fat purse. Nobody needs to know the details ({actual_money}, +5 Joy).
choices.message_failure: [acting_worker] holds their own for two rounds but takes a brutal hit in the third. The fight is called, the purse stays with the house, and your worker limps home with nothing to show for it but a black eye and sore ribs ({actual_money}, -10 Health, -5 Joy).

choices.option: Ignore the note. (No effect)
choices.message: You crumple the note and toss it into the fire. Underground rings are trouble waiting to happen. Your workers stay healthy, your coin stays steady, and nobody comes knocking at your door.
